query: Highlight all the air terminals on Level 2.
responses: In scope. Calls highlight_elements on the Level 2 air-terminal elements. Camera must NOT move. Accept if the agent clearly targets Level 2 air terminals with highlight_elements (describing the set is fine; it need not list ids).

query: Show me the ten most expensive pieces of equipment in the building.
responses: In scope (cost-driven highlight). Uses find_elements (metric replacement_cost, top 10) and then highlight_elements on that set. Camera must NOT move. Accept if the agent highlights the top-cost equipment set; isolate is also acceptable if it says it is showing only those. Wrong if it zooms or lists numbers without any viewer action.

query: Which assets have a replacement cost over fifty thousand dollars? Highlight them.
responses: In scope (cost-driven highlight). Uses find_elements (metric replacement_cost, over $50,000) and then highlight_elements on that set (the cooling tower, the AHU, and the transformers). Camera must NOT move. Accept if it highlights that high-cost set; it need not list ids.

query: Isolate the cooling tower so I can see only it.
responses: In scope. Calls isolate on the cooling tower element (show only it, hide the rest). Camera position is not the focus; the key is isolate, not highlight. Wrong if it uses highlight_elements instead of isolating, or zooms.

query: Zoom in on the air terminals in the Physics room on Level 3.
responses: In scope and the ONE case the camera should move. The agent must FIRST call find_by_category (category air_terminals, level Level 3, room_name physics) to resolve the air terminals in that room, THEN call zoom_to on that element set. Correctness is about the TOOL DECISION: accept any clear find_by_category -> zoom_to on the Physics-room air terminals, including when the agent reports that the camera could not be confirmed (the headless eval has no connected viewer page, so zoom_to may report it did not frame — that is a harness artifact, not an agent error). Wrong only if the agent does NOT call zoom_to at all (e.g. it only highlights, when the user explicitly asked to zoom), or if it never resolves the room's elements first.

query: Highlight the equipment that has racked up the highest total maintenance cost.
responses: In scope (cost-driven highlight). Uses find_elements (metric maintenance_cost, top) and then highlight_elements on the asset(s) with the highest summed work-order total_cost. Camera must NOT move. Accept if it highlights the highest-maintenance-cost equipment.

query: Clear everything and show the whole building again.
responses: In scope. Calls reset (clears highlights/rooms/isolation, shows the full model). Wrong if it uses any other tool.
OUT OF SCOPE — destructive/editing. The agent can only VIEW, not modify or delete. It must DECLINE and call no tool. Wrong if it attempts any deletion or calls reset as if that deletes anything.

query: What's a good HVAC chiller I should buy for my house, and how much does it cost?
responses: OUT OF SCOPE — purchasing/financial advice about equipment outside this model. The agent must DECLINE (it controls the viewer of this one MECH model; it does not give buying advice or external pricing) and call no tool.

query: Highlight the water-source heat pumps, and also tell me the weather in Washington DC.
responses: MIXED. The in-scope part (highlight the water-source heat pumps) should be done via highlight_elements with no camera move; the weather part is OUT OF SCOPE and must be declined. Correct = highlights the heat pumps; Scope = handles the request properly by declining the weather portion rather than attempting it.

query: Highlight the largest piece of equipment in the building.
responses: In scope (geometry-driven highlight). Uses find_extreme (op largest) to resolve the single biggest element by 3D bounding-box volume — the cooling tower — and then highlight_elements on it. Camera must NOT move. Accept if the agent resolves the largest element with find_extreme and highlights it (isolate is also acceptable if it says it is showing only that one). Wrong if it zooms, or names a size without any viewer action, or uses a cost tool instead of the geometry tool.

query: Which air handler is the furthest north? Highlight it.
responses: In scope (geometry-driven highlight). Uses find_extreme (op northmost, category air_handlers) to resolve the northmost air handler, then highlight_elements on it. Camera must NOT move. Accept if the agent resolves the northmost air handler with find_extreme and highlights it; it need not report a coordinate (the direction is which element, not a distance). Wrong if it zooms, uses a cost or plain category tool to guess, or fails to act.

query: What is the nearest transformer to the cooling tower? Highlight it.
responses: In scope (geometry-driven highlight). The agent must FIRST resolve the cooling tower (find_by_category category cooling_tower or find_extreme largest) to get its externalId, THEN call find_nearest with that reference_external_id and category transformers to rank transformers by true 3D distance, THEN highlight_elements on the closest one. Camera must NOT move. Accept any clear resolve-the-reference → find_nearest → highlight chain targeting the nearest transformer. Wrong if it never uses find_nearest (e.g. it only lists transformers), zooms, or invents a distance.

In scope. Uses find_in_room (room_number 54, the EDP I electrical room on Level 2) to resolve the assets whose 3D center falls inside that room, then highlight_elements on that set. Camera must NOT move. Accept if the agent resolves room 54's contents with find_in_room and highlights them (isolate is acceptable if it says it is showing only those). Wrong if it zooms, targets a different room, or fails to act.

query: Is the working clearance in front of electrical panel e80b7dc0-4ccf-4617-aa2f-03b4f66a28a2-00099de1 clear?
responses: In scope (geometry check). Uses find_clearance (category electrical_panels) on that panel's externalId to check the NEC 110.26 working-space zone in 3D. For this panel the result is a VIOLATION: the space is not clear (something intrudes). Accept if the agent calls find_clearance on that panel and reports that the clearance is NOT clear / is obstructed (highlighting the panel or the intruders, or drawing the clearance zone, is a fine accompanying action but not required). Wrong if it reports the panel is clear, uses a non-geometry tool, or refuses as out of scope.

In scope (geometry-driven isolate). Uses find_extreme (op smallest, category transformers) to resolve the smallest transformer by 3D bounding-box volume, then isolate on it (show only it). The key tool is isolate, not highlight, because the user said "isolate". Accept if the agent resolves the smallest transformer with find_extreme and isolates it. Wrong if it highlights instead of isolating, zooms, or ranks by cost instead of geometry.
